title: Milo's Cafe: a neighborhood site with a live patio
tag: Café and restaurant website, Morrisville, NC
summaryLead: A one-page café site that answers three questions: what is on the menu, are you open, can we sit outside.
summaryMore: Hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a live patio scene from the free Open-Meteo weather service.

stack.name: Delivery
stack.detail: One self-contained HTML file. No framework, build step or database.

stack.name: Accessibility
stack.detail: HTML5 landmarks, ARIA tabs, live regions and a name on every control.

stack.name: Type
stack.detail: Newsreader for headlines, Hanken Grotesk for body.

stack.name: Menu
stack.detail: 69 items as structured data, with search, a meat-free filter and guest favourites.

stack.name: Patio scene
stack.detail: Inline SVG driven by time of day and weather. Falls back to the day's hours if the request fails.

stack.name: Ordering
stack.detail: Buttons link to the café's SpotOn page. No cart on the site.

chapters.title: A patio you can check first
chapters.challenge: A photo cannot say whether today is a patio day.
chapters.solution: An SVG scene driven by time and weather, with a verdict and a day slider.
chapters.outcome: A quick answer to "should we sit outside?", refreshed every 30 seconds.

chapters.title: A menu that is data, not a PDF
chapters.challenge: PDF menus cannot be searched and are hard to read on a phone.
chapters.solution: 69 items rendered into tabs with live search and a meat-free filter.
chapters.outcome: Found in seconds, and a seasonal change is a one-line edit.

chapters.title: Help for the undecided
chapters.challenge: First-timers face dozens of items with no starting point.
chapters.solution: A "pair it" tool picks a food and drink combination by mood.
chapters.outcome: A low-pressure way in, with no account or tracking.

results.title: Answers up front
results.text: Hours and the patio verdict sit in the top bar, with a sticky Order and Call bar.

results.title: A usable menu
results.text: Real text that search engines and screen readers can read.

results.title: Motion that respects people
results.text: Intro, cursor, marquee and count-up are skipped for reduced motion.
